key_insight: A feature-based manifold model can predict the transient wake dynamics of actuated bluff-body flows with an analytical, control-oriented reduced state instead of relying on POD modes and unsteady training data.
engineering_relevance: This provides an interpretable surrogate for flow control design, enabling fast prediction of how time-varying actuation affects wakes in configurations such as the fluidic pinball.
method: Replace POD modes with a feature-based manifold of the same dimension
Build the state space from dynamic features that encode coherent structures
Augment the state space to capture transient responses to arbitrary actuation
evidence_signal: The model is validated on the fluidic pinball at Re=30 against several representative actuation scenarios and is reported to accurately reproduce transient dynamics without unsteady training data.
watch_item: The approach is demonstrated on a specific low-Re canonical bluff-body case, so robustness and tuning requirements for more complex geometries or higher-Re flows may still need verification.
paper_title: Feature-based manifold model of actuated wakes
